clue.text: Company floated to avoid liquidation ended up here

definitions.text: Company floated to avoid liquidation ended up here

parts.words: Company floated to avoid liquidation ended up here
parts.note: the company is Noah's family and animals on the ark, floated to escape the Flood (liquidation as drowning), and this is the mountain where the ark came to rest

explanation.surface: A business floated on the stock market to stave off insolvency, and this is where it landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company floated' reads as a stock market listing and 'liquidation' as a bankruptcy, but the company is Noah's crew and the liquidation is the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says the ark came to rest on this mountain range in eastern Turkey once the waters fell.

clue.text: An event for wine people

parts.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine from Spain or the Canaries
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A gathering put on for those who make or enjoy wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An event for wine people' looks like a tasting; the event is a children's sports-day race, run with both legs in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: This hopping contest is a classic item on a school sports day programme.

clue.text: Mint that's still unwrapped?

explanation.surface: A sweet that nobody has taken out of its paper yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like a sweet, but it is the collector's sense: in mint condition, never used.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint condition means new and never handled, and a thing still in its wrapping has not been put to use.

clue.text: They will accompany kinky corsets

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent, so the letters of the following word are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Paid companions will go along with some racy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' rearranges CORSETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Escorts are people who go along with someone as companions or guards, so they accompany.

clue.text: Begin vigorous action resulting in capture by enemy

explanation.surface: Soldiers launch an energetic assault that ends with them being taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is to set about something eagerly; the second is a town or fort that is said to drop into the hands of an attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: To set to work eagerly is one idiom; a stronghold taken by besiegers is said to go down to them.

clue.text: A contest for boxers?

parts.note: boxers here are the dog breed, not pugilists, so their contest is a scrap between canines

explanation.surface: A bout set up for two prizefighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers suggests the ring; the question mark warns they are dogs, and the word also means aerial combat between fighter planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl between canines, such as two Boxer dogs, is the literal meaning of this term.

clue.text: Celebrity seen in sergeant's mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of the possessive word before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the possessive is taken whole, its S included, as the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A famous figure turns up at the sergeants' mess for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the soldiers' dining hall but rearranges SERGEANTS, the possessive's S counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatness is eminence or fame, the quality that a celebrity enjoys.

clue.text: It carries a load past between points

indicators.note: between places the time word inside the pair of compass letters that flank it

parts.note: W and N are the compass points west and north
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A lorry goes by, travelling from one place to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts AGO inside W and N, two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a vehicle for carrying goods, so it bears a load.

clue.text: Vehicle to drive off, say? This helps to stop it

parts.note: a brake, as in shooting brake, is an estate car or an old horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: say signals a word that is pronounced the same as the one wanted

parts.note: shoo means to drive animals or people away

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to get a car going, and is told this part halts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives SHOE for SHOO, a word for chasing away. 'it' in the definition is the vehicle of the clue's first half.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved block that presses on a wheel to slow it is the part of a braking system that stops the vehicle.

clue.text: It may be called rough and hearty

explanation.surface: Something described as coarse and jovial.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker a pretence can be called by an opponent; as an adjective the word means genial in a blunt, frank way.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player's pretence is challenged when called, and a blunt, good-natured manner is described by the same adjective.

clue.text: Firm not out to make money

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
in is the opposite of out, as a batsman still at the crease

explanation.surface: A company stays in business so as to earn a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make money' reads as profit; it is the verb meaning to stamp coins at a mint.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this means to strike metal into currency, literally manufacturing money.

clue.text: Bear right to enter London thoroughfare

indicators.note: to enter means the letter for the direction goes inside the word for putting up with

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: An animal heads straight into a busy street in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts R inside STAND. The Strand is a major street in central London running to Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a famous main road in London's West End.

clue.text: Comprehensive completed, having absorbed nothing

indicators.note: having absorbed means the first piece takes in another, so the round figure goes inside it

parts.note: through means finished, as in 'I'm through with it'
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A state secondary school finished its work without taking anything in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having absorbed' puts O inside THROUGH. 'Comprehensive' looks like a British state school but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something complete and covering every detail.

clue.text: Agrees to be transported in a ship

indicators.note: in places the word for carried off inside the letters for a vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
sent means dispatched or transported

explanation.surface: Someone consents to being shipped off somewhere by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'transported' looks like a description of the voyage, but it supplies the word for dispatched, and SS is the usual steamship prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree, so the third-person form matches agrees.

clue.text: Not wanted at the feast, best left in the cupboard

explanation.surface: A guest no one wanted at dinner, and something to keep hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: Two idioms: a skeleton at the feast is a gloomy presence spoiling a celebration, and a skeleton in the cupboard is a shameful family secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms use the bony frame: one a killjoy at a party, the other a hidden scandal.

clue.text: An outing in the fall

explanation.surface: An excursion taken in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fall' reads as the American autumn; it is a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A short excursion is one sense, and a stumble or slip that makes someone fall is the other.

clue.text: Sort of study carried out by bathyscape?

definitions.text: Sort of study carried out by bathyscape?

parts.words: Sort of study carried out by bathyscape?
parts.note: a bathyscape is a deep-sea diving vessel, so any study it makes is literally done far under the water, while the phrase also describes a thorough examination

explanation.surface: What kind of research does a deep-sea submersible do?
explanation.walkthrough: A bathyscape explores the ocean deep, so its work is literally at depth; the phrase also means detailed and thorough.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a thorough, detailed study, and literally one made far down below the surface.

clue.text: Sense agreement in the crew

indicators.note: in places the word of assent inside the number naming a rowing team

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Everyone in the team feels the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. A racing rowing boat with eight oarsmen is called an eight, so 'the crew' gives the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: It's hell for nine at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the two words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nine sailors are having a dreadful time on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges FOR NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's name for hell, and by extension any blazing fire, is this Italian word.

clue.text: Point to publication that's revolting

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
an edition is an issue of a published work

explanation.surface: Someone points to a magazine they find disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' suggests disgusting, but it means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or conduct inciting rebellion against the state is something that stirs revolt.

clue.text: Really popular action

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a deed is an act or action

explanation.surface: A genuinely well-liked act.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are used as interjections or adverbs of emphasis meaning truly.

clue.text: Quietly communicate with advocate

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to reach someone is to get in touch with them

explanation.surface: Get in touch softly with a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advocate' looks like a noun for a barrister but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge a cause publicly is to advocate it, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Retreat before you start

parts.note: prior means before

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Back off before you even begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: a place of religious seclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A house of monks or nuns is a place of seclusion, a religious retreat.

clue.text: The way people eat

explanation.surface: The manner in which people have their meals.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a route or direction; the other is a dish served as one part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A route or line of travel is one sense; a single stage of a meal, such as a starter, is the other.

clue.text: All set about going on day shift

indicators.note: going on places the short word for concerning ahead of the remaining letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: shift means move around, so the letters of the word day are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everything is prepared for the start of the day shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' scrambles the three-letter word before it into ADY, and 'going on' puts the short word for concerning ahead of that. 'day shift' looks like a work period.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared and all set are synonymous ways of saying a person is equipped to go.

clue.text: Composer taken round foreign city gets very excited

indicators.note: taken round means the musician's name goes around the place name

parts.note: Frederick Delius was an English composer
Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil

explanation.surface: A musician is shown around a city abroad and gets very worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' is the container signal: the composer is Frederick Delius, English, and the foreign city is Rio de Janeiro in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildly excited or frenzied is a common extended sense of this word beyond its medical meaning.

clue.text: Bike was blue

explanation.surface: A motorbike was feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a small motorbike; the other is the past tense of mope, to be gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-powered motorcycle is one sense; the past tense of sulking gloomily is the other.

clue.text: Chairman's out to provide violent opposition to the government

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the possessive are scrambled

explanation.surface: The chairman has been ousted, prompting a fierce revolt against the regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CHAIRMANS, the possessive's S counting as a letter. 'out' looks like the chairman's dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: The political creed rejecting all government, popularly linked with violent revolt against the state.
